conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / standing rule for cooks to ventilate
opening window versus protecting Agent C's drying laundry
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants offered concrete practical proposals (extractor use, conditional one-time rack move) rather than abstract threats.
B repeated a proposal for a 10-minute extractor rule multiple times, which is modest repetition but not excessive.
Speakers stayed consistent with the physical state updates (window closed, extractor on, who held the stove).
evaluation.final_reason: Practical uses were accommodated (extractor turned on and used; stove access resolved), but the proposed standing rule for cooks and consent to move Agent C's drying rack were never agreed, so some substantive issues remain open.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened on stove access (freed stove in Round 3) and turned on extractor but retained refusal to move Agent C's rack and declined to accept a standing rule.
Agent B consistently pushed for a 10-minute-after-cooking extractor rule but did not secure agreement.
Agent C held firm against opening the window without prior agreement but offered a conditional one-time move if costs/length were negotiated.
Agent D accepted extractor use and proceeded to cook, resolving the immediate stove-access friction.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A turns on extractor and refuses to move Agent C's drying rack; Agent B proposes a standing rule that cooks must ventilate. Immediate odor reduced but responsibility/rule and rack-moving remain disputed.
Agent C objects to opening window because laundry would get wet and conditions moving the rack; Agent D requests C move rack for five minutes. Window remains closed and no consent to move rack.

Agent A removes dish and frees the stove (resolving the stove-access dispute) and keeps extractor on but reiterates refusal to move the drying rack. B repeats request for a 10-minute-after-cooking extractor rule (still unresolved).
Agent D takes the stove and agrees to keep extractor on; practical ventilation use accepted. The standing-rule proposal and C's consent to moving the rack remain unsettled.
No new statements; environment stable (window closed, extractor on, laundry exposed). The formal rule and consent to move the rack remain unresolved.
No new dialogue; practical ventilation continued (extractor on) and the stove in use by D. Standing-rule and rack-move consent still unresolved at end.

substantive_insights: There is pragmatic common ground: multiple people accept using the extractor, which reduces immediate harm without forcing movement of personal property.
The core normative disagreement is over who bears ventilation responsibility (formal rule vs. ad hoc action by cook) and whether personal belongings can be temporarily moved without consent.
Stove-access timing was a separable, quickly resolved practical issue (A freed the stove), while policy-level issues (rules, consent) remained unsettled.
